newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian defence ministry sues weekly for libel.
newsitem.headline: Croatian defence ministry sues weekly for libel.

text.p: Croatia's defence ministry sued a leading independent weekly for libel over a report saying that the government had sheltered a Bosnian Croat wanted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal, state agency HINA said on Tuesday.

Globus weekly reported in October that Ivica Rajic, a militia leader linked to the 1993 massacre of 16 Moslem civilians, had lived in a hotel owned by the Defence Ministry in the port city of Split for almost a year.
It published pictures purportedly showing Rajic near the hotel reading a newspaper.

"It is a flagrant lie that the published pictures showed Ivica Rajic and it is equally untrue that the Defence Ministry has been in any contact with Rajic or that it has been helping him to hide," the ministry said in the suit.
The ministry said earlier the man in the Globus pictures was a hotel maintenance worker. It also denied Globus claims that official intelligence sources had informed the paper of Rajic's whereabouts.

Croatia armed Bosnian Croats in their 1993-94 separatist war against the Moslem-led central government. Bosnian Moslems and Croats are now in an uneasy federation held together by U.S. diplomatic pressure.

Croatia passed special legislation on cooperation with the international war crimes tribunal (ICTY) in April in which the country committed itself to extraditing indicted war criminals found on its territory.
But only one Croat suspect surrendered to the ICTY while all others remain at large.
The tribunal has so far indicted over 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for atrocities, but only seven are held in its custody.
